[[Category:Logic]]
'''Truth table''' is an aid for assessing the validity of composite statements via analysing the relationship between the composite [[statement]] and its substatements.

{{Hidden example}}

$$
P: \text{If students work hard in class, they will always get good grades.}
$$

Is [[statement]] $P$ true?

'''Solution''':

First break $P$ down into its substatements and rewrite in formal symbolic logic language:

$$
\text{A: Students work hard in class}\\
\text{B: Students get good grades}\\
\text{P:A} \implies \text{B}
$$

Then construct the '''truth table''':

{| class="wikitable"
! A !! B !! P: A $\implies$ B
|-
| T || T || T
|-
| T || F || F
|-
| F || T || T
|-
| F || F || T
|}

Therefore, it can be concluded that $P$ is true if and only if there is never a situation where A is true but B is false, i.e., there is never a student that worked hard in class but did not get good grades.
{{End hidden}}

=== Formal definition of a truth table ===

$$
f:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}^m\\
T=\{(x,f(x)) \mid x\in\{0,1\}^n\}
$$

$f$: arbitrary boolean function

$T$: truth table
